summary: ADR-025 §D9 says alarm payloads are "identifiers and enums only" — the shipped payload also carries a timestamp
description:
ADR-025 §D9 (docs/adr/ADR-025-admission-events-and-offline-reconciliation.md:193) reads: "Occurrence ids and alarm payloads carry bounded identifiers and enums only — no buyer, no guest reference, no raw scanner-operator identity (ADR-003 §D3)."

The shipped admission-conflict payload carries `device_occurred_at` (a timestamp) and `skew_flagged` (a boolean) alongside its four UUIDs — services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:297-304. A timestamp is neither an identifier nor an enum. The policy-conflict payload likewise carries `version` (an int) and `revisable` (a bool) — scan.go:305-315.

Nothing is wrong with the code: §D5 REQUIRES the device-claimed time to be recorded, so device_occurred_at is mandated by the same ADR whose §D9 wording excludes it. The defect is in the decision record.

Why it matters rather than being pedantry: §D9 is the PII contract a future consumer or reviewer implements from. A strict reading rejects every schema-1 alarm we emit today, and a reviewer applying §D9 literally to a new field would reach the wrong verdict. The wording should name what the floor actually is — bounded identifiers, enums, and operational scalars (timestamps/flags) that are not attributable to a person — while keeping the prohibition (buyer, guest reference, raw operator identity) unchanged.

This is an ADR amendment, so per the sdlc skill it could go straight to the default branch — EXCEPT that settling what the PII floor admits is a decision, not a transcription, and the plan gate is where a wrong recommendation gets reversed. Hence a ticket.

Source: TKT-86 ai-review second pass (gpt-5.6-sol), finding P3 — triaged INCIDENTAL. Pre-existing: the timestamp shipped with TKT-85, and §D9's wording predates it.
